turns.content: The state is (-1,2,1)^T and the observable is P=[[0,1/sqrt(2),0],[1/sqrt(2),0,1/sqrt(2)],[0,1/sqrt(2),0]]. Find a vector spanning P's zero-eigenvalue eigenspace.
Normalize the zero-eigenvalue eigenvector found above and verify that applying P gives zero.
Normalize the state (-1,2,1)^T and state its squared norm before normalization.
Take the inner product of the normalized state with the normalized zero-eigenvalue eigenvector and compute the scalar needed for the Born-rule probability.
Check whether the projection amplitude and all outcome probabilities satisfy Born-rule normalization, and state the zero-outcome probability.
Verify the norms of the state and zero-eigenvalue eigenvector, and distinguish the projection amplitude from its squared Born-rule probability.
Report the probability of obtaining the zero outcome.
